title: Every PR plays an HDR copy in a real browser and copies a 4K TrueHD film
description: JS-025's HDR copy is checked in a browser only with E2E_HEVC=1, which CI's Chrome cannot use, and its 4K TrueHD criterion rests on one manual measurement. CI's Chrome plays AV1, so an AV1 HDR10 copy can be played there; and a 4K copy is cheap enough to time on CI's two cores.
acceptanceCriteria: An e2e scenario plays an AV1 HDR10 film with audio the browser does not play from a copy in CI's Chrome: master VIDEO-RANGE=PQ, ffmpeg copying the video, currentTime advancing through a seek
An integration test copies a synthetic 4K HDR10 HEVC film with 5.1 TrueHD through the worker's own ffmpeg and checks it runs well above real time on two CPUs, with hvc1, PQ kept and stereo AAC
An integration test copies AV1 HDR10 through the worker's own ffmpeg and checks the init segment keeps the PQ transfer and the master's range
Both run in CI without E2E_HEVC and without a GPU
notes: JS-025's reviewers found the HDR copy path untested in CI's browser and the 4K TrueHD criterion unchecked. The lead measured 30 s of 4K HDR10 HEVC with TrueHD copied in 0.41 s on 4 CPUs, so a timing bar has a wide margin even on two cores. Priority 3, ahead of JS-026, because it closes a criterion of a done task. Built 2026-11-09, tests only: an e2e scenario plays an AV1 HDR10 copy in CI's Chrome (PQ master, ffmpeg copying, a seek to an unbuffered point); a 4K HDR10 HEVC film with 5.1 TrueHD copies at 55x real time on two pinned CPUs (bar 10x); an AV1 HDR10 copy keeps PQ in the init segment's colr box. QA's warm-repeat hunt caught the scenario assuming playback starts at 0 (a rerun resumes); the lead made it seek to an unbuffered point (6 of 6). The first run used a stale copy of the workflow without the tier gate; resumed from the repository's build.js.
